translation_notes: context shim: the three `from nanopub.* import ...` lines retargeted to a local nanopub_context.py (HYCL, NanopubConf, Profile, ProfileError, the dummy nanopub namespace); identical for both sides

context shim: `from nanopub_context import super` -- the region is a constructor of NanopubClaim(Nanopub); extracted as a module-level function, CPython's zero-argument super() has no __class__ cell, so the name is shadowed by a stand-in recording super().__init__(conf=conf); identical for both sides
the two self.assertion.add((...)) calls, which share a subject, merge into one graph island with a `;` predicate list; the single provenance add becomes a one-line island
Literal(claim) -> {claim} inside the island (node() coerces a str to the same Literal); URIRef(self.profile.agent_id) -> f<{self.profile.agent_id}>

RDF/RDFS/HYCL -> rdf:/rdfs:/hycl: prefixes; the whole `from rdflib import RDF, RDFS, Literal, URIRef` line and `from nanopub_context import HYCL` disappear on the ldpy side (term-construction scaffolding absorbed by the notation)

IMPORTANT negative finding: Nanopub.assertion and Nanopub.provenance are READ-ONLY properties, and ldpy's only graph-mutation idiom is the augmented assignment `G += g{...}`, which needs an assignable target; the translation therefore has to call `self.assertion.__iadd__(g{...})` explicitly. A non-assigning form (something like `G.add(g{...})`) is missing from the notation; the driver's stub reproduces the read-only properties so this is actually exercised

this_statement = self._metadata.namespace.claim stays Python: the namespace is a runtime attribute of the nanopub metadata, not a lexically known prefix, so the subject is interpolated as {this_statement}
the `not self.profile` branch (raise ProfileError) is not covered by a fixture: the harness reports a raised exception as an execution error, not as a comparison
